blocks.heading: Why intervene in business activity?
blocks.text: Government may intervene because business choices can affect people who do not participate in the transaction, because workers or consumers may need protection, because competition and information may be imperfect, or because access to essential services and development objectives may not be met by commercial incentives alone. Intervention can use rules, incentives, public provision or information. It also uses resources and can create compliance costs or unintended effects, so explain the problem and whether the measure addresses it. A private profit is not proof of social harm, and the existence of regulation is not proof it works.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Omi Blocks can increase profit by leaving costly dust control out while nearby residents bear cleaning inconvenience. The decision shifts some consequences outside the firm’s own accounts, giving a reason to consider protection. A suitable response should reduce the stated dust rather than simply punish unrelated activity.
